Type with a purpose

Instructional measure

Bell Gothic Black gives headings their voice. Inter carries the reading and interface text. Magda Clean Mono identifies literal values and code. Purpose sets the font, size, and rhythm.

Reading

Room to think

Good interfaces leave room for the work. A clear heading establishes the subject; a steady rhythm carries the details. Emphasis has a purpose. The rest can feel quiet and considered.

A steady reading rhythm

Article text shares one reading color, including links, lists, and inline code.

  • Give each idea room.
  • Keep nested emphasis at the same text opacity.

Clear typography lets the writing lead.

Approved defaults

A useful record of the work

A technical note should make its next step easy to find. Start with the decision, explain the constraint, and leave enough room for the reader to follow the example. Emphasis marks the important part. An aside can remain quiet and readable.

Use deployment_id when referring to a literal value. Follow the type reference for the roles behind this page.

Keep the details intact

  • Let prose wrap; preserve the spacing of code.
    • Scroll long code lines without widening the document.
  • Keep links underlined without requiring hover.
  • Expose the full value when a compact label is truncated.

The same words should remain usable at a different size.

Long tokens can wrap without widening the page: deployment_production_us_east_01_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789.

const deployment = {
  id: "deployment_production_us_east_01_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789",
  region: "us-east-1",
};

Type reference

Headings use Text with an explicit heading element. Article links and code use native HTML inside Prose. Outside an article, literal values use Text’s code variant.

request.duration_ms

Keyboard notation is presentational: . It does not register a shortcut.
